On non-CVMs, requires hatch_avatar_video_api; when the gate is off, returns an empty array before reading avatar state or resolving media. kind=avatar_dance_video selects the active default Jolly’s unexpired bundled dances, the active ready-made Halloween look's six cache-backed dances, or the published final audio outputs of settled custom-avatar dances, with music resolved through get_audio. Only the active look's missing videos and paired frames are downloaded on demand; missing cache roles yield no attachment, without generating videos or showing plain Jolly instead. Every entry carries kind=avatar_dance_video, matching gallery attachments. Six complete dances return six attachments; base clips and final paths associated with multiple dance/aspect-ratio pairs are omitted. Optional audio.audio_asset_id carries the resolved song asset ID without the song:// prefix. A successful no_audio_configured result returns the final video without audio metadata. Missing kind returns an empty array without reading avatar state or resolving media. Unsupported kinds return 400. Music lookups are deduplicated by saved reference and share one 30-second deadline with at most six concurrent calls. Completed results are retained at expiry; unfinished or missing videos and failed or timed-out music lookups are omitted. If every lookup fails or times out, returns an empty array with HTTP 200. Default dance expiry_time is an exclusive UTC Unix-second cutoff evaluated at request start. Reads never generate videos, probe video streams or persist music metadata. Approval IDs are account-scoped on today's single-account runtime: authenticated identity claims establish account access, while the daemon mirror and Sentinel's atomic pending checkout check gate the selected approval. A supplied expected_payment_revision must match the displayed revision; omission preserves legacy selection behavior. Stale supplied revisions return 409 without changing the approval. Retry only with the same Idempotency-Key and destination.daemon_avatar_media_getStream the file for one avatar asset slotStreams the file the manifest lists for one slot: `asset` (an id the manifest lists), `part` (`still` or `video`) and `appearance` (`light`, `dark` or `alpha`), with optional `switch` as on `GET /api/avatar/assets`. The full-size file is served through the raw file routes (`ETag`, ranges and `HEAD`) and named in `X-Avatar-Asset`, `X-Avatar-Part`, `X-Avatar-Appearance` and `X-Avatar-Revision`. With `p`, a `/fs/thumbnail` preset (`default`, `compact` or `whatsapp`, `sm`, `lg`, `image_thumb`), it serves that slot's thumbnail exactly as `/fs/thumbnail` does, a video's from its first frame: from the shared cache with the thumbnail's `ETag`; on a miss, a GET waits up to 3 s for generation, then 202 with `Retry-After: 5`, or 503 with `Retry-After: 10` when the queue is full; 404 for a file type with no thumbnail; 400 for an unknown preset or `p` on an alpha video slot, whose thumbnail decoder cannot preserve alpha. With `rendition` (`240` or `480`, the longest edge in pixels) on a `video` part, it serves a smaller H.264 copy of the slot's video, named in `X-Avatar-Rendition`: made the first time it is asked for, then streamed from a cache through the raw file routes until the video changes; on a miss a GET gets 202 with `Retry-After: 5` while it is made, or 503 with `Retry-After: 10` when that queue is full, and a HEAD gets 404 `not_ready`. `rendition` with a `still` part, an `alpha` appearance or `p` is 400 `invalid_query`. Requires `abra_hatch_avatar_assets_api` (404 `not_enabled` otherwise); 503 `registry_unavailable` (not retryable) when this build's asset registry did not load. A `dark` request whose slot has no file yet is served the slot's `light` file, with `X-Avatar-Appearance: light` and the dark slot's status in `X-Avatar-Status`; `alpha` never falls back. 404 `not_ready` when the slot isn't ready (for `dark`, nor its `light` slot), with its status in `X-Avatar-Status`; 404 `unknown_asset` when the manifest lists no such asset or part; 400 `invalid_query` names a missing or malformed parameter. A read can request dark mode assets, as on `GET /api/avatar/assets`.image/pngvideo/mp4video/webmThe slot's file or thumbnaildaemon_avatar_assets_getGet the avatar asset manifestEvery asset of the owner's avatar with its still and video in each appearance (light, dark, alpha), each part's status and files, and family completeness: the same response for every caller, which maps its states to assets itself. Requires `abra_hatch_avatar_assets_api`; returns 404 `not_enabled` otherwise, and identity then carries no `avatar.assets_revision`. The only query parameter is `switch`: `display` serves the avatar the display still shows while a new one isn't ready (`avatar.switching`), `immediate` (the default) the active avatar; other parameters and custom request headers are ignored. `ETag` is the revision, with a `.display` suffix for `switch=display`, so a matching `If-None-Match` returns 304 with no body. 400 `invalid_query` means a bad `switch`; 409 `avatar_changed` means the activation moved mid-read; 503 `state_unreadable` comes with `Retry-After`; 503 `registry_unavailable` (not retryable) means this build's asset registry did not load, and identity then carries no `avatar.assets_revision`. With `hatch_avatar_dark_mode_assets` on, a read of a custom avatar whose portrait has no dark file marks it as owing dark media, which avatar completion then makes; the response itself never changes.unknown_assetthe manifest lists no such asset or partthe avatar state could not be read; keep the last manifestportrait.basesize overflows MAX_SIZEevent
